title: OneNote on iPhone: Copilot chat pane with page summaries and Q&A
summary: Hold: the briefing leaves an existing way to disable Copilot unconfirmed, although Microsoft documents connected-experience controls for OneNote on iOS. The rollout and licence-assignment instructions are supported, but the inference about there being no new data store is not established.

claims.claim: Assign the product licence in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the **Billing** > Licenses page.
2. Select a product.
3. On the product details page, select **Assign licenses**.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a product licence to a user.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.

claims.claim: The cited Copilot admin-center settings page lists no setting named for OneNote.
claims.quote: Searched: OneNote in the complete fetched Configure Microsoft Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center page. Its user access, data access, actions, other settings and app-experience sections name no OneNote setting.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraphs; Open questions: first bullet
claims.claim: Which existing Copilot setting can switch off this pane for a group of licensed users is not confirmed.
claims.quote:
If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps:

- Excel
- OneNote
- Outlook
- PowerPoint
- Word
claims.fix: Remove the first Open questions bullet and replace the unconfirmed-switch sentence with: 'Turning off connected experiences that analyze content makes Copilot features unavailable in current OneNote apps on iOS; this is a broader control, not a pane-only switch.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy. The following sentence on that page explicitly includes iOS. For group targeting, https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/privacy/ios-privacy-preferences names the Cloud Policy setting 'Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content', and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy documents scope to specific groups. Do not add a control row.

claims.claim: The exposure follows existing permissions rather than a new store of data.
claims.quote: Searched: OneNote Copilot interactions stored history prompts responses iOS iPhone. Read MC1307979 and copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy; access restrictions do not establish this storage inference, and the latter documents stored OneNote Copilot interactions.
claims.fix: Delete 'rather than from a new store of data'. The notice supports the existing-access boundary but does not establish that storage conclusion.

claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks admins to review is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Review sharing on notebooks that hold sensitive content, because the notice says the pane draws on content the user can already open. / The only controls row is licence assignment.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'Review sharing on notebooks that hold sensitive content'. It asks admins to check a control absent from the table; do not add a row.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits the briefing's verified facts and the action scale on 25 November 2026.
claims.quote: action: "prepare" / risk: "medium" / defaultState: "on" / decide whether anyone who uses OneNote on iPhone should gain or lose it before the end of November 2026
claims.fix: Change action from 'prepare' to 'act-now': the automatic end-of-November rollout is within about 60 days of 25 November 2026, the page rates risk medium, and it asks for a licence decision before rollout.
